name: showreel-c3-menu-spacing

voice.text: This menu is costing them customers. Turns out, it's not the colours. Fix one: line every item up to one edge. Fix two: one font, in two weights. Fix three: double the space between groups. Same words. Now it looks twice the price.

caption:
This menu was costing them customers. Three fixes, same words. ☕

1. Line every item up to one edge. Centred lines each start somewhere new, so the eye has to hunt.
2. One font, in two weights. Four fonts read as noise; one font with a bold and a regular reads as a plan.
3. Double the space between groups. Space tells the eye what belongs together.

Save this for your next menu, slide or poster. Which fix would you do first?
keywords: how to make a menu look expensive

sources.title: Proximity Principle in Visual Design (Nielsen Norman Group)
